title: Dapagliflozin reduces intracellular sodium and induces osmotic diuresis in cardiac myocytes.
abstract: Dapagliflozin is a selective SGLT2 inhibitor. SGLT2 is encoded by SLC5A2 gene. In human proximal tubule cells, dapagliflozin inhibits SLC5A2 and decreases sodium-glucose reabsorption, leading to natriuresis and osmotic diuresis. This lowers plasma volume and relieves hemodynamic burden in heart failure.

title: Renal hemodynamic effects of SGLT2 inhibition: activation of tubuloglomerular feedback.
abstract: Inhibition of SGLT2 by dapagliflozin increases distal sodium delivery to the macula densa, which activates tubuloglomerular feedback. This induces afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction and decreases intraglomerular pressure, protecting against chronic kidney disease progression.
